fields.description:
Sibling of cabc-7a98-d173-4d7c, found in its Phase-1 sibling sweep (E5). Jira DC's shared pager
`_paged_search` loops on `startAt` offsets with no stall guard. A server that ignores/repeats
`startAt` (returns the same page) spins forever — measured: 26 calls to the experiment harness cap
— instead of terminating loudly. Same defect class as cabc (Cloud acli_graph cursor spin, fixed by
ab7f in 30c522cde9) and `fetcher._iter_pages` (guarded since bug deac).

CORRECTED LOCATION: the original description cited `adapters/jira/transport.py:379-416`. Ticket
465d's one-module-per-capability split has since landed and moved the pager verbatim to
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py:120-157` (`_TransportBase`,
the shared pager every capability mixin inherits).

## Proven root cause (runtime-confirmed; full RCA in the ticket comments)

M1 — `_base.py:141-157`: the pager's ONLY loop exit is `if not batch: break`. `start_at` advances
locally but nothing verifies the SERVER honoured it, so an offset-blind instance re-serves the same
non-empty page forever and the exit is unreachable (`out` grows unbounded). Runtime evidence: a
`startAt`-ignoring stub drove 26 calls, requesting offsets [0,3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,27,...] while
receiving page 1 every time; terminated only by the harness cap.

M2 — `_hierarchy.py:91`: `get_parent_map` wraps the drain in a bare
`except Exception: warn; return {}` degradation contract, which converts any pager-level abort into
a SILENT empty parent map. Runtime evidence: the same stub returned `{}` after 26 calls, raising
nothing. So M1's loud signal is neutralised at this caller unless re-raised ahead of the broad clause.

Legitimacy = defect, against cited authority: `fetcher.py:336-344` (the same operation on a
parallel surface raises `SilentTruncationError(reason="offset-stall")`, contract stated at
`fetcher.py:275-277`), `acli_graph.py:29-46, 79-86` (the Cloud sibling raises
`RunawayPaginationError` and its readers re-raise past fail-open at `acli_graph.py:304-306`), and
the prior CLOSED `Fixed:` bug cabc for this same class.

## Plan

Deliberately narrow: ticket 465d owns re-architecting these modules and another stream owns
`set_parent`/parent handling, so the diff touches only the guard, its one re-raise, the facade
re-export, and the test.

1. `_base.py` — define `RunawayPaginationError(RuntimeError)` beside the pager (local to the DC
   adapter, no cross-adapter coupling to Cloud's `acli_graph`). In `_paged_search`, remember the
   previous page's first issue key; if a page repeats it, raise — the server is not honouring
   `startAt`, so paging can never advance. Fires on the SECOND call.
   DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from `fetcher.py:335-345`: fetcher returns cleanly (no raise) when the
   repeated page is SHORT, reasoning a client that returns fewer items than asked and then repeats
   "has nothing further to give". That does NOT transfer to DC. This pager exists (bug 9263)
   precisely because a hardened DC caps EVERY page below the requested size via
   `jira.search.views.default.max` — so on DC a short page is the NORMAL case WITH more to give, and
   adopting fetcher's short-page branch would silently return 20 of 250: the exact 92%-loss defect
   this pager was built to refuse. `_paged_search` therefore raises on ANY repeated page, short or
   full. It cannot false-positive: a `startAt`-honouring server serves DIFFERENT issues per offset.
2. `_hierarchy.py` — add `except RunawayPaginationError: raise` immediately ahead of
   `get_parent_map`'s broad `except Exception`, mirroring `acli_graph.py:304-306`.
3. `transport.py` — re-export the error through the existing `__all__` facade (2 lines; no other
   change to that file, which 465d owns).
4. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py` — the RED oracle.

## Verification

RED→GREEN with the oracle held out from the implementing subagent, plus a defect-seeded mutation
check (re-remove the guard -> the test must return RED). Then `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the
DC + fetcher + acli_graph pagination suites.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_paged_search` raises a dedicated runaway/stall error when `startAt` does not advance
- [ ] Fail-open exception handling does not swallow the stall error (it must propagate)
- [ ] Held-out test with a `startAt`-ignoring stub proves termination within 2 calls
- [ ] Existing DC pagination behaviour for well-behaved servers unchanged (250/250 still recovered
      from a page-capping client through all three whole-project readers)
